options.title: Protecting Reserve Beds
options.description: Implement a policy to protect a certain number of monitored beds for acute arrivals, especially CTAS 1 and 2 patients.
options.local_fit: This option directly addresses the observed pattern of CTAS 2 patients not having immediate access to monitored beds due to high bed occupancy. It ensures that a designated number of beds are reserved for these critical patients.
options.possible_pressure_transfer: Pressure may shift to the role responsible for managing bed allocation, as they will need to ensure compliance with the new policy. Additionally, there might be increased pressure on the triage team to accurately assess and prioritize patients.
options.how_we_would_know: Monitor the number of CTAS 2 patients with immediate access to monitored beds after implementing the policy. Compare the results to the baseline data to determine the effectiveness of the intervention.
options.revisit_or_stop_if: If the new policy does not significantly improve access to monitored beds for CTAS 2 patients, or if it leads to unintended consequences such as increased wait times for other patient categories.

options.title: Escalation Huddles
options.description: Establish escalation huddles triggered by wait-time thresholds, particularly for room-to-physician waits, to address slow physician pace and potential capacity issues.
options.local_fit: While this option has not been directly tested in the local context, it could help address the observed slow physician pace and the resulting pressure on the system. It provides a structured approach to managing capacity issues.
options.possible_pressure_transfer: Pressure might shift to the role responsible for coordinating and facilitating the escalation huddles. Additionally, there could be increased scrutiny on the physician team's performance during these huddles.
options.how_we_would_know: Monitor the number of escalation huddles triggered and their impact on reducing wait times. Compare the results to the baseline data to assess the effectiveness of this intervention.
options.revisit_or_stop_if: If the escalation huddles do not lead to significant improvements in wait times or if they become a burden on the physician team, causing delays in patient care.

recommendation.rationale: The leading option, 'Protecting Reserve Beds', directly addresses the observed pattern of high bed occupancy and slow physician pace impacting CTAS 2 patients' access to monitored beds. While the evidence strength for this option is low, it has a strong local fit and could provide immediate relief for CTAS 2 patients.
recommendation.would_change_if: If further analysis reveals that the slow physician pace is a more significant contributing factor, the leading option might shift to 'Escalation Huddles'. Additionally, if the high bed occupancy is found to be due to a temporary surge in patient volume, a different approach might be warranted.

suggested_reviewers.why: The Bed Management Team is responsible for ensuring efficient bed utilization and has insights into the challenges of high bed occupancy.
The Physician Lead can provide insights into the challenges of slow physician pace and the potential impact of escalation huddles.
